A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
an increase in soil temperature is likely to promote the transfer of Cd and Pb to plants in contaminated soils.
the soil-to- plant transfer of metals is not necessarily promoted by a rise in temperature.
a rise in soil temperatures may lead to a decrease in metal bioavailability and a concomitant increase in their transfer to plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil-to- plant transfer of metals in agricultural soils can be predicted by taking into account the temperature-induced changes in soil DOM.
the soil-to- plant transfer of Cd and especially Zn in the contaminated agricultural soil studied here is not likely to be altered by the global warming.
the bioavailability of Cd and Zn is expected to be reduced by 10–20 % in a warmer climate.
